title: OneDrive Photos on Windows: policies for personal account sign-in and app blocking
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap target from Microsoft's later rollout notice. The documented policy paths and registry/CSP values check out, and the notice supports their applicability to Photos; the briefing appropriately leaves Photos-specific licensing and personal sign-in defaults unresolved.

claims.claim: The OneDrive photos shown in Photos are photos stored in OneDrive.
claims.quote: Moments: For photos saved in OneDrive, revisit memories with “On this day”, themed collections, and automatic seasonal recaps.

claims.quote: Review your existing Windows app-management and OneDrive policies, especially rules that intentionally block or remove Photos.

claims.claim: The cited Intune path is Devices > Configuration > Create > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Create > Basics > Next > Configuration settings > Add settings > OneDrive.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Configuration > Create. ... Platform: Select Windows 10 and later. ... Profile type: Select Settings catalog. ... Select Create. ... In Basics ... Select Next. ... In Configuration settings, select Add settings. ... select OneDrive

claims.claim: Enabling DisablePersonalSync sets HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive, DisablePersonalSync, to DWORD 1.
claims.quote: Enabling this policy sets the following registry key value to 1: [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: The Intune Basics step requires a Name before selecting Next.
claims.quote: In Basics, enter the following properties: Name: Enter a descriptive name for the profile. ... Description: ... This setting is optional, but recommended. ... Select Next.

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync is a user-scope HKCU registry policy.
claims.quote: ## User Configuration policies ... ### Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts ... [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps is mapped to Computer Configuration and Windows Components > Store in Group Policy.
claims.quote: Name | DisableStoreApps ... Friendly Name | Disable all apps from Microsoft Store ... Location | Computer Configuration ... Path | Windows Components > Store

claims.claim: The CSP URI ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ApplicationManagement/DisableStoreOriginatedApps accepts integer 1 to disable app launch.
claims.quote: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ApplicationManagement/DisableStoreOriginatedApps ... Format | int ... 1 | Disable launch of apps.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps is a computer-scope policy.
claims.quote: Scope ... Device ... Location | Computer Configuration

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: The Store policy turns off launch of all pre-installed or downloaded Microsoft Store apps, not just Photos.
claims.quote: Disable turns off the launch of all apps from the Microsoft Store that came pre-installed or were downloaded.

claims.claim: Apps are not updated when the Store policy disables them.
claims.quote: Apps won't be updated. Your Store will also be disabled.

claims.claim: Learn documents DisablePersonalSync in terms of OneDrive sync rather than Photos.
claims.quote: This setting lets you block users from signing in with a Microsoft account to sync their personal OneDrive files.

claims.claim: Learn documents DisableNucleusSync as the registry value for Prevent Lists sync from running on this device.
claims.quote: Prevent Lists sync from running on the device: [HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive] "DisableNucleusSync" = "dword:1"

claims.claim: The Lists policy name is DisableListSync, different from its DisableNucleusSync registry value.
claims.quote: This policy's registry value name DisableNucleusSync differs from the policy name DisableListSync.

claims.claim: Enabling the documented Lists policy blocks Lists sync from running on the device.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, Lists sync will be blocked from running on the device.

claims.claim: The cited Lists sync policy page does not mention Photos.
claims.quote: Searched: Photos in the full fetched Use Group Policy to control Lists sync settings page (https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/lists-sync-policies). Read the complete page; it documents Lists sync and DisableNucleusSync but does not mention Photos.

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync can be configured through Group Policy or Intune.
claims.quote: ### Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts ... Applies to: Group Policy, Intune
